name: Aveiro
title: Aveiro Ultrasonic Thickness Gauging | Bulkers and Coasters
description: Thickness measurement at the port of Aveiro: bulk carriers, general cargo coasters and fishing vessels, holds, tanks and decks gauged alongside or at the yard.
h1: Ship Gauging and Hull Thickness Measurement at the Port of Aveiro
intro: Aveiro's port sits at the Gafanha peninsula on the edge of the Ria de Aveiro, a lagoon system on Portugal's Atlantic coast. Bulk carriers, general cargo coasters and a working fishing fleet call here, and a local shipyard gives vessels a place to dock. Gauging fits berth stays and yard periods. Atlantis NDT mobilises ultrasonic thickness technicians from India to join the ship.

highlights.p: Coastal bulk carriers and general cargo ships discharge fertiliser, building materials and cargo here. Holds are empty after discharge, which is the best time to gauge coamings, tank tops and frames.
Aveiro has ship repair capacity for coasters and fishing vessels, so a gauging team can work to a docking programme and measure shell plating while the vessel is out of the water.

highlights.h: A bar and a shallow lagoon
highlights.p: The entrance bar and channel depths shape which ships can call. Smaller coasters are typical, and gauging windows depend on tide and weather, so planning begins from the agent's schedule.

port.h: Aveiro, the Ria and the ships that call
p: Aveiro lies about midway down Portugal's Atlantic coast, and its commercial port is on the Gafanha peninsula, a sandy strip between the Atlantic and the Ria de Aveiro. Ships reach the quays by a dredged entrance channel through the bar at the harbour mouth, and then along a channel into the lagoon. The entrance is exposed to Atlantic swell, and in heavy weather the bar can be closed to shipping. Depths in the channel are limited, so the port suits small and medium-sized ships rather than ocean-going giants.

Traffic centres on bulk and general cargo. Coastal bulk carriers bring cereals, fertiliser, cement and other building materials, and break-bulk and project cargo arrive on multipurpose coasters. A ro-ro and container flow runs on a smaller scale, and Aveiro's industrial hinterland, which includes ceramics, paper and metal fabrication, feeds some outbound cargo. The Gafanha area has a long fishing tradition, and fishing vessels, trawlers and support boats use the harbour basins and yard. Tugs and pilot boats handle the movements through the channel.

Planning depends on tide and weather. Ships entering the port plan around the state of the tide and a forecast that keeps the bar open, so arrivals can shift by a day or more. Once alongside, the stay for discharge is usually a few days, which gives time for hold gauging after the cargo is out. Fishing vessels and coasters moving to the yard offer a longer window, because a docking allows shell, rudder and propeller areas to be measured. We build the plan around an agent's updates and keep a flexible start date so a delayed arrival does not waste the mobilisation.

facilities.h: Where gauging can be done at Aveiro
p: The port has a ship repair yard serving coasters, fishing vessels and workboats, and this is the place where bottom and side shell gauging out of the water is possible. Navalria is the yard name usually associated with the port's shipbuilding and repair, and ships docked there can have shell plating, sea chests and the rudder and propeller area measured with staging and access arranged by the yard. Ships too large for the yard's facilities dock elsewhere in Portugal or in Galicia, and Aveiro then supports the gauging afloat before the move.

At the cargo quays, holds on bulk carriers and coasters can be gauged once discharge is complete and the holds are cleaned and ventilated. Tank spaces on small tankers or general cargo ships with ballast tanks are accessible when the crew has emptied and released them. Fishing vessels at lay-by berths are gauged for owners who want a condition check ahead of a survey or a sale. Access to each berth and to the yard is arranged through the ship's agent, and each compartment is entered only under the ship's own permit system.
list: Cargo quays at Gafanha — hold, coaming and tank-top gauging on bulk carriers and coasters after discharge.
Ship repair yard on the lagoon — shell, sea chest, rudder and propeller-area gauging during dockings of coasters and fishing vessels.
Lay-by berths — owner's condition gauging of idle coasters and fishing vessels.
Ro-ro and container berth — deck, ramp and ballast-tank readings on small short-sea ships.
Fishing harbour basins — hull and tank gauging on trawlers before surveys or sales.
Pre-docking calls — afloat gauging that feeds steel estimates for yards in Aveiro, Galicia or elsewhere in Portugal.

context.h: Port state control and the rules around Aveiro
p: Portugal participates in the Paris MoU, and port state control inspections at Aveiro follow the same risk-based method as elsewhere in the region. They are carried out under the Directorate-General for Natural Resources, Safety and Maritime Services, abbreviated DGRM, while the local harbour master's office handles day-to-day maritime administration. Older coasters with a history of structural wastage are inspected more often, and a recent gauging report lets the superintendent see what an inspector might find in holds and ballast tanks.

EU regulations influence small-ship owners as well. The EU ETS has covered shipping since 2024 and FuelEU Maritime has applied since 2025, though smaller coasters fall outside parts of both, depending on tonnage. The EU Ship Recycling Regulation asks for an Inventory of Hazardous Materials on ships calling at EU ports. For Aveiro's typical customers, the main driver for gauging is the class survey cycle and the commercial decision to renew steel or retire an older hull. Fishing vessels follow their own flag-state and class requirements, and we scope their gauging accordingly.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs at Aveiro
jobs.p: Aveiro jobs are mostly small-ship work. The superintendent or owner supplies the last gauging record and the survey due date, and we agree whether the work will be afloat at a cargo quay or tied to a yard period. Typical requests:
list: Hold, coaming and tank-top plating gauging on a coastal bulk carrier after discharge, for an intermediate or renewal survey.
Shell plating, sea chest and rudder-area gauging on a coaster in the yard's dock, with readings fed to the class surveyor.
Ballast-tank and deck gauging on a general cargo ship at a lay-by berth ahead of a sale.
Condition gauging of a fishing vessel's hull and tanks before a survey or a transfer of ownership.
Re-gauging of renewed plating after yard repair, to confirm the new steel against drawing thickness.

logistics: The nearest international airport is Porto's Francisco Sá Carneiro, with Lisbon an alternative for longer connections; both are reachable by road. Technicians from India travel through a European hub. The ship's agent arranges port and yard access and any launch needed. Portugal is in the Schengen area, so Schengen visas are obtained in India before departure, and the application starts once the arrival or docking date is firm and the owner has supplied an invitation letter. Because bar conditions can move arrival dates, travel is confirmed against the agent's most recent update.
vessels: Small short-sea container and ro-ro ships

faqs.q: Is there a drydock at Aveiro?
faqs.a: The port has a ship repair yard that serves coasters, fishing vessels and workboats, and it is where shell gauging out of the water is realistic. Larger ships dock elsewhere in Portugal or in Galicia. We confirm with the owner whether the target vessel fits the yard before planning the mobilisation.

faqs.q: What decides when a ship can be gauged at Aveiro?
faqs.a: Mostly the tide, the bar and the cargo programme. A ship arrives when the entrance is open and the draught allows, and discharge decides when holds are empty. We follow the agent's updates and keep the start date flexible, so a delayed arrival changes the plan without losing the stay.

faqs.q: Can holds on a bulk coaster be gauged at the quay?
faqs.a: Yes, once discharge is complete and holds are cleaned and ventilated. We gauge tank tops, lower frames, bulkheads and hatch coamings, taking readings against the ship's thickness records. Cargo residue can hide corrosion, so the crew usually sweeps and washes before gauging begins.

faqs.q: Do you gauge fishing vessels at Aveiro?
faqs.a: Yes. Hull plating, tank boundaries, fish-hold structure and deck areas can be gauged afloat or at the yard, depending on access. Owners often ask for this ahead of a survey or sale, and the report is structured by compartment so it can be shared with the buyer, the class surveyor or the yard.
